Hi Aisha,

Thanks for taking this — we need a concise, ops-ready recommendation for how Redwood can support our data residency and deletion obligations for PHI. High level: MedInsights will process patient data in both the EU and US. Our legal team requires that patient identifiers (name, SSN, contact) be purged or irreversibly redacted after a configurable window. We also need the ability to keep de-identified clinical transcripts for analytics up to 7 years.

Specific asks:
- Can Redwood implement a per-tenant retention window that enforces automatic permanent deletion of raw PHI fields after N days?
- Are there supported patterns for field-level redaction (e.g., redact name/SSN but keep anonymized clinical notes)?
- Is there a safe approach for sampling-based deletion (e.g., keep only 10% of raw records beyond the retention window for research) while still meeting GDPR/UK-GDPR requirements?
- We need proofs: audit logs, deletion receipts, and one-line operational playbook we can include in procurement.

Attached the SLA request packet and a spreadsheet with the fields we consider PHI. Can you loop in the right infra/security folks and confirm a timeline for an initial playbook?

Appreciate it,
Lydia

Hi Lydia — quick technical summary / recommended patterns we typically propose for regulated PHI customers (short bullets so you can paste into the SLA packet):

- Retention tiers by data class:
  - Raw identifiers (name, SSN, contact): configurable retention window; recommend default N=90 days for production ingestion unless legal requires otherwise.
  - De-identified clinical transcripts (PII removed / hashed): retain up to 7 years for analytics.
- Deletion modes:
  - Soft delete (metadata flag + revoke access + 30 day quarantine): useful for approvals workflows.
  - Hard delete (irreversible purge): immediately remove model inputs, input-level KV caches, and VPC-hosted object stores; we produce a deletion receipt (signed event) with timestamp and object ids.
- Backups & snapshots:
  - For Redwood Private deployments: we can disable offsite backups or configure retention windows aligned to the tenant policy; for Hosted API we support scheduled purge and certified deletion windows but some cloud snapshots may have provider-level retention — we document that in the playbook.
- Redaction approaches:
  - Field-level redaction: canonical approach is to strip identified fields at ingestion via a pre-processing pipeline (regex + named entity model), then store both raw and redacted versions in separate stores. Raw is subject to hard-delete after window.
  - Deterministic pseudonymization/hashing: keep stable pseudonyms for research cohorts (salted, KMS-backed salt per-tenant); combine with access controls and separate keys for re-identification to satisfy legal controls.
  - Token-level redaction: for tokenized input we support policy-based token masking in the serving runtime to avoid KV cache leakage of sensitive n-grams.
- Sampling-based retention (research cohorts):
  - We support cohort sampling as an explicit policy: tag records at ingestion with sampling flags, move sampled set to a long-term analytics store (de-identified), and hard-delete remainder. This requires documented consent/legality; we recommend a consent & record-keeping pattern in the playbook.
- Auditability & evidence:
  - Deletion receipts (signed event ID + timestamp) for every hard-delete operation.
  - Per-tenant audit logs for access and deletion operations, exportable via secure link.
- Operational playbook (1-page):
  1) Ingestion: pre-process -> tag PHI fields -> store raw in encrypted bucket (Private only) + redacted copy in analytics store.
  2) Retention enforce: daily job checks retention clock -> hard-delete raw objects -> emit deletion receipts -> append to audit log.
  3) Sampling: on policy date, move sampled cohort -> run additional de-id -> retain per analytics TTL.
  4) Validation: weekly audit job to verify no raw PHI in serving caches.

Notes on model serving / caches (Marcus will add config details): ensure per-route policies disable persistent KV cache for PHI routes and set per-request caching TTLs to zero when redaction is required.

If you want, we can include a short appendix describing how Redwood Private helps (tenant-managed KMS, backup control, no provider-managed snapshots).

—Priyom
